answer: One quill can scrawl a thousand names, but a stake-weighted quorum prices influence in locked capital, not identities. An agent's bond sets its voting weight, so splitting one purse into a thousand fake keys buys no extra power: divided coins still sum to the same weight. Each new vine of identity needs a minimum stake, so mass registration burns real funds. A public beacon flags coordinated double-signing, and slashing destroys every posted bond. The attacker must lock capital equal to the influence sought and risks losing it all, so a one-third attack costs a third of the economy.
